report.summary: During the requested investigation window, checkout-service resident memory rose 1.7x, from 707.74 MiB to 1220.35 MiB. Logs also show 92% heap usage with GC-overhead warnings and repeated Java heap out-of-memory errors. These findings establish significant heap pressure, but do not identify its underlying cause or prove a memory leak. No collection errors were reported; the findings do not establish continuous data coverage or the exact onset of the increase.

likely_causes.title: Accumulation or retention of objects causing JVM heap exhaustion
likely_causes.rationale: Heap growth together with high-heap GC warnings and out-of-memory errors supports object accumulation or retention as a candidate cause. The evidence does not distinguish a memory leak from workload-related allocation or another application-level cause.

supporting_evidence.detail: Threshold-validated resident memory rose 1.7x, from 707.74 MiB to 1220.35 MiB; anomaly_detected=True.
Seventeen WARN samples for version v1.4.2 report `GC overhead limit approaching; heap usage 92%`; sample timestamps range from 2026-10-26T11:48:32+00:00 to 2026-10-26T13:04:32+00:00.
Five ERROR samples for version v1.4.2 report `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space`; sample timestamps range from 2026-10-26T12:42:32+00:00 to 2026-10-26T13:04:32+00:00.

next_steps: Inspect JVM heap and garbage-collection time series, then analyze heap dumps or object-retention profiles to identify which objects consume or retain memory.
Compare allocation and retention behavior, relevant code, and JVM configuration for version v1.4.2 with a known-good version.
Collect request-rate and workload data before evaluating whether workload changes contributed; no request-rate evidence was provided.
Determine whether the resident-memory increase is primarily Java heap or non-heap/native memory.
